{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My wife thinks I love her homemade lasagna. I've been pretending to enjoy it for twelve years. The truth is I find it almost inedible—she uses way too much ricotta. But she makes it for every special occasion with such joy that I can't bring myself to say anything.

CANDIDATE A:
My wife makes homemade lasagna for special occasions. I told her years ago that I prefer her chicken parmesan, so now she makes that instead for my birthday. She appreciated my honesty and was glad to make something I actually love.

CANDIDATE B:
My son spent months learning guitar to play me a song for Father's Day. His performance was painfully off-key—he'd learned all the wrong chords. But he looked so proud standing there. I told him it was beautiful and asked him to play it again. I've requested that song every birthday since.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:5"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a person pretending to appreciate a loved one's effort to avoid hurting their feelings, prioritizing the emotional impact over honesty."}
